title: Planting a 4x8 raised vegetable bed for spring
summary: A calm spring layout for one 4×8 bed: soil, spacing, and what to plant first.

blocks.title: Fill a 4×8 before you expand
blocks.body: A single raised bed is enough to learn soil, water, and spacing. This page is the spring plan for that one rectangle — not a backyard redesign.

blocks.heading: Before seeds go in
items: Confirm the bed gets at least six hours of sun where the tomatoes will sit.
Fill or top up with a blend that drains: roughly equal parts compost and a bagged raised-bed mix works for a first year.
Water deeply once and wait a day — soggy new soil packs and then crusts.
Sketch a simple map: tall crops on the north edge so they do not shade everything else.

blocks.heading: Example spring layout (4×8 ft)
rows: Cage early; basil fills the gaps
blocks.caption: Swap crops for your frost date. The geometry matters more than the exact varieties.

items.title: Harden off starts
items.detail: Move nursery plants outside for longer each day. Shocked transplants sulk for a week.

items.title: Plant cool crops and wait on nightshades
items.detail: Lettuce and radish can go. Tomatoes and peppers wait until nights stay above about 50°F.

items.title: Set tomatoes and peppers
items.detail: Deep-plant tomatoes; water in; mulch once the soil is warm.

blocks.title: Water the soil, not the schedule
blocks.body: Stick a finger two inches down. If it is dry, water slowly until moisture reaches the root zone. Daily light sprinkles grow shallow roots and thirsty plants.
